title: RootFab 4D BioWeave: Gene-Activated Periodontal-Ligament Stem-Cell Constructs for Autonomous Root-surface Regeneration, Shape-Memory Dynamics and Long-Term Functional Integration
content: Current periodontal therapies rarely rebuild the hierarchical cementum, periodontal ligament, or bone complex that stabilizes teeth under loading. This Review introduces RootFab 4D BioWeave, a materials–first framework that integrates stem cells, 4D bioprinting and gene activation for autonomous root–surface regeneration. The platform employs a trilayer, anisotropic GelMA and PCL scaffold reinforced with bioactive phases to reproduce native gradients and guide cementogenesis. Shape-memory programming enables conformity to defect topographies, while staged gene-activation payloads, from transient mRNA to inducible CRISPRa/i plasmids, coordinate cell behavior. A central theme is closed-loop mechanogenetic control. A piezoelectric mesh converts masticatory forces into electrical signals that, after rectification and conditioning by downstream electronics, provide timed cues that gate transcriptional programs and coach tissue maturation during function. We synthesize design rules that connect scaffold anisotropy, piezoelectric output, and shape-memory behavior to periodontal outcomes, and we outline translational and safety considerations for combination products. The goal is durable restoration of a load-sharing, sensorimotor-competent periodontal complex.
